speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, I would clarify the issue of the Deed of Gift between the executors of the estate of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew and the National Heritage Board (NHB), as I was then the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I would elaborate on due processes for proposals on the conservation and preservation of properties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, let me touch on the Deed of Gift.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From early 2015 onwards, NHB started planning for a major SG50 exhibition on 6 August 2015, just before the Jubilee Weekend.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Following the passing of Mr Lee Kuan Yew in March 2015, NHB was also in discussion with the executors of the estate about a donation of artefacts from 38 Oxley Road which could be incorporated into the exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Deed of Gift was not based on NHB's standard agreement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Members would have heard just now, the Deed of Gift required NHB to display only part of the demolition clause in Mr Lee's will.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, NHB was to display the first part, which sets out Mr Lee's wish to demolish the house, but not the second part, which sets out his wish should the house not be demolished.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At that time, NHB did not pick up the significance of this partial quote from the demolition clause.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Lee Suet Fern, who was then the Director on the Board of NHB, was also involved in the discussions between NHB and the executors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She supported the conditions stipulated by the executors in the Deed and, her law firm, Morgan Lewis Stamford LLC, helped in the process of finalising the Deed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The executors held firm to many of the terms they had stipulated in the Deed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, when NHB asked to amend the $1 buyback provision, the lawyer for the executors stated that this clause was non-negotiable.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While the terms were unusual, NHB proceeded to sign the Deed with the executors because it recognised the heritage significance of the artefacts and felt that it would be in the public interest for them to be exhibited.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At around the same time, I updated the Prime Minister on the plans for the exhibition and the inclusion of the Oxley Road artefacts in the exhibition, including the conditions stipulated in the Deed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I later shared with him a copy of the Deed on 12 June.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As the Prime Minister shared earlier, he felt that the terms of the Deed were onerous to NHB and he told me that, as a beneficiary of the estate, his consent for the donation had not been sought, the executors had not informed him of the donation nor the terms of the donation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It had signed the Deed and had accepted the gifts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it was not clear if the executors were properly empowered to enter into the Deed without first consulting all beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This also raises questions about the validity of the agreement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Moreover, the planned exhibition was just two months away and NHB did not have much time left to resolve the issues and then properly prepare for the exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I discussed this with the then CEO of NHB Ms Rosa Daniel to see what could be done about the matter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Given the circumstances, we agreed that it would be better to take a pause and not rush the Oxley Road items for the August exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We could exhibit them at a later stage, after the issues had been resolved.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I asked Ms Daniel to inform Mr Lee Hsien Yang that we would like to put off the display of the Oxley Road artefacts from the August exhibition and do so at some time in the future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, NHB had no intention to breach any legal obligation and Ms Daniel clarified this point in an email to Mr Lee Hsien Yang the next day.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She said that the Minister's instructions are that NHB is not to breach its obligations if it has entered into valid agreements which are binding on it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While the executors were insistent that NHB had to follow through on the exhibition, NHB still had the duty to check whether the Deed of Gift was in order in light of the different views of the beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, NHB wrote to the lawyers of the executors to clarify whether probate had been granted for the will, whether there were any other beneficiaries entitled to the assets of the estate and, if so, whether the consent had been obtained for the gift to NHB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Before responding to these queries, the executors of the estate put out a media release on 11 June publicising their donation of items to NHB.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was a surprise to NHB because the queries had not been addressed.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, NHB issued a statement that same night to highlight that there remain some questions on the Deed of Gift which NHB was in the process of clarifying with the executors.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He also said that NHB should not be concerned about the position of the beneficiaries under the will.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this response still left open the question of whether there were, indeed, other beneficiaries and whether their consent had been sought for the donation of items to NHB for the exhibition under the stipulated conditions.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Throughout this period, I was discussing the matter with Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean as the Prime Minister had said that he would leave it to the Deputy Prime Minister to handle the specific dealings between NHB and the executors on the Deed of Gift.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo's main concern on the conditions was that NHB was being asked to display a partial quote of the demolition clause which did not fully reflect Mr Lee Kuan Yew's wishes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He felt that NHB, as a public institution, should remain neutral and should not be drawn into a private disagreement or be used to present a particular point of view which was incomplete.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was a major SG50 exhibition on our founding leaders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had artefacts not just from the estate of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew but also from the National Archives and the families of other founding leaders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And many of these artefacts had not been displayed before.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The artefacts helped to enhance the storyline of the exhibition and to bring out the values of our founding leaders for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Subsequently on 25 June, the Prime Minister informed me that he had written to the executors, in his capacity as beneficiary, indicating to them that notwithstanding his position on the Deed of Gift, he would not object to the exhibition as he did not want to put NHB in a difficult position.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As NHB needed more time to prepare, it sought the consent of the executors to push back the exhibition date.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, I attended the opening with Mr Lee Hsien Yang, Dr Lee Wei Ling and Ms Lee Suet Fern.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The exhibition was very well received, and it has been extended till now.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If Mr Lee Hsien Loong has asked for the Deed of Gift in his private capacity, NHB would have been entitled to give it to him, given his position as elder son and beneficiary of the estate.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More generally, in a scenario where items are being donated to NHB from an estate, and NHB becomes aware that one of the beneficiaries objects to the terms of the donation, it would be necessary for NHB to take steps to verify that there is agreement from all beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Otherwise, it could face a potential claim from a beneficiary whose consent was not given.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this case, Mr Lee Hsien Loong told me that his concern was not with the donation of artefacts to NHB but rather the way it was handled and the terms of the donation, as he had shared in his speech earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite his personal reservations over how the artefacts were conveyed to NHB by the executors in the Deed of Gift, the Prime Minister did not instruct me to stop the display of the Oxley Road artefacts in the exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, he asked me to take instructions from the Deputy Prime Minister on the matter and that was how the matter was handled.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, Madam, I have given an account of what happened to the NHB Deed of Gift.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Contrary to this being an abuse of power, I believe the matter was handled correctly and above board.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government undertakes a vigorous assessment process for all such properties before deciding whether or not to conserve or preserve them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will elaborate briefly on what this process is.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, Government agencies will undertake detailed research on the preservation or conservation merits of the property of interest.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Agencies will have to review the historical, cultural, social and heritage significance of the property, its national importance as well as its architectural merits and rarity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In examining the historical significance of a site, for example, NHB will review how the site has played a role in our national history.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In examining the architectural merits of the building, the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) will study which parts of the building are most architecturally significant, or, if it is a cluster of buildings, which are the most significant buildings within the cluster.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, agencies would look into the planning considerations of the property and its surroundings.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes examining whether there are any technical regulatory requirements which may have an impact on the form of preservation or conservation proposals for the property.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Agencies will also review the allowable uses of the site.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, URA may look at whether a conserved residential building can be adapted for commercial use or for civic and community purposes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But such a change in use will have to be compatible to its surroundings and supported by infrastructural considerations, such as a potentially higher traffic count brought about by the change of use.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Arising from these planning studies, agencies may then review the need for the Government to acquire the property for conservation or preservation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But beyond the legal requirement, the question is whether the planning intent for the conserved or preserved site is best served by having the Government owning the site as opposed to leaving it under private ownership.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, if the intent for the site is to have significant public access and the owner is not prepared to do so, then one option is, indeed, for the Government to acquire the site.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Agencies will engage and undertake these sorts of research work to provide the baseline information we need for all such properties.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there is a need to decide on the next step for the property, then the Government agencies will proceed to seek views from the relevant stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, views will be sought from the property owner.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Views will also be sought from relevant professionals and subject matter experts.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The URA has a conservation advisory panel while the NHB has a preservation of sites and monuments advisory board.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The advisory panels comprise professionals in the building, arts and heritage and education sectors, and will provide their inputs on the conservation or preservation proposals tabled by the agencies.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: URA and NHB will submit the recommendations of their findings to the respective Ministries for decision thereafter.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If the Government, acting through the Ministry of National Development (MND) or the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth, decides to pursue the conservation or preservation proposal, the property owner will be given the opportunity to respond and appeal.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Based on past cases, the vast majority of owners would agree with the conservation or preservation proposals.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A few have appealed but the final decision for conservation or preservation lies with the Government.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, prior to the formation of the Ministerial Committee, various agencies have already been working on this issue.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: NHB has been documenting the historical significance of the house.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MND and URA have been looking at options for the property as well as the planning and zoning implications arising from the different scenarios.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This work was being done at the staff level.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the right and responsible thing to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many baseless allegations have been made against the Government and I hope this debate will give us a chance to discuss the issues openly, dispel doubts and strengthen confidence in our public institutions and system of government.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Above all, we will continue to uphold the values of Mr Lee Kuan Yew and our founding leaders and do our utmost to serve Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We will take all clarifications after the speeches.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Other critical and crucial ancillary issues raised include allegations of abuse of power and the manipulation of our State Organs by our Prime Minister and the Cabinet.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: On the issue of 38 Oxley Road, public opinion has been deeply divided.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: One, why has the Government set up a Ministerial Committee to consider options that may differ from the personal wishes of the late Mr Lee?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Two, why is this issue being debated in Parliament?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They say any dispute over the last will and testament of Mr Lee should be a matter placed for judicial decision between the estate, executors and beneficiaries.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Many of my residents have shared their views with me on whether 38 Oxley Road should be demolished.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Whether one agrees with or is opposed to the demolition of 38 Oxley Road is a matter of opinion, and valid, reasonable arguments prevail on both sides of the aisle.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: However, whether 38 Oxley Road should be demolished is not up for debate today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The allegation made is that steps taken by the Government to consider preserving 38 Oxley Road in any form or manner are invidious, aimed at furthering sinister political ends.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There is a Chinese phrase that I keep in mind whenever a complex conundrum of an ethical nature confronts me and that is "合 情 合 理 合 法".

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: That is, to see if the action taken was reasonable, logical and legal.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: If any action meets all these three criteria, then more likely than not, it is an ethically sound one.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Lee Kuan Yew was the Founding Prime Minister of our country.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our history, the odds and obstacles we faced and how far we have come bears no repeating today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Supporters or detractors alike, there is no one in Singapore who can reasonably deny the crucial role Mr Lee played in bringing Singapore from Third World to First.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Lee played the role of a Founding Prime Minister of a country post-Independence, not unlike Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of India or Chairman Mao Zedong of China.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Citizens of these respective countries may not all subscribe to the politics or personalities of these political figures, but they stand for more than just their political or personal beliefs.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Their place in a nation's history cannot be replaced and should not be forgotten.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This was clearly evident during his passing and funeral in 2015.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Lee stood for the fundamental values of what Singapore represents − multiculturalism, meritocracy, good governance, rule of law, the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am sure all Singaporeans agree with me when I say that the ideals of these values associated with Mr Lee should be passed down to latter generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Preserving 38 Oxley Road is one way to do so.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I grant detractors that it is not the only way or may not be the best way to do so, but I am of the respectful and humble view that it will be a great dereliction of duty of any Singapore government of the day not to even consider the possibility of doing so.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the United States, their very first President, George Washington's home at Mount Vernon, Virginia, was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1960 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Therefore, what we must ask ourselves is this: is it reasonable, logical, legal, that is, 合 情 合 理 合 法, for our Government to set up a Ministerial Committee to consider the possibility of preserving the home of Mr Lee?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: All things considered, the answer must be yes.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Some Singaporeans say that Parliament is not the place to settle family disputes.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: A simple answer is that we are not doing so today.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We are here because the integrity of the Prime Minister and our Government has been called into question and Singaporeans have a right to know the full details of these allegations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: How then is this different from all the other allegations made by many others over the years?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: My sense from speaking with Singaporeans on this issue is that the perception of credibility is higher because of the individuals making the allegations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Dr Lee Wei Ling and Mr Lee Hsien Yang are children of the late Mr Lee and siblings to the Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Being family members to two of our Prime Ministers suggests that they are in a position to know or possess information that ordinary Singaporeans may not.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But there is this public perception, the perception that allegations made by the Prime Minister's siblings or family may be more credible than others.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: A formal national forum, such as a Parliamentary debate, is ideal to address these allegations.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is important because such allegations have far-reaching implications, not only about the decision to demolish a house, but the integrity and reputation of the Singapore Government is at stake at home and abroad.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Amidst an uncertain world and a volatile economy, nothing can be more important.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We all hope that this matter will be resolved with finality after this debate.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There is, therefore, a likelihood that further rebuttals and counter-allegations will continue in social media and the press after this debate concludes.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is sadder still that this whole saga is centred on Mr Lee's will because his wish on 38 Oxley Road is well-known.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The opinions of the WP members and Members of Parliament (MPs) on the other aspects of the issues are just as diverse as public opinion has been in these few weeks.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: As an outsider to this dispute, I personally believe that the acrimony between the Lee descendants has much deeper roots than just the fate of the house arising out of the will.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: This is because all sides seem to be willing to risk the national interest by bringing this private matter into the public domain.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: This is a fundamental point that I want to make which I personally feel strongly about.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: We need to restore the line, make it a bright red line, resolve the aspects of disputes that have crossed into the public domain and push the dispute back into the private domain.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is also the foundation of Singapore's unforgiving anti-corruption stance.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Unfortunately, in this whole saga, I personally think that the line has been blurred and crossed many times by all sides.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: First, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling should not make vague allegations in the public domain against the Prime Minister based on scattered evidence centred on family displeasure.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Making allegations that appear to be calculated to undermine the Prime Minister's authority does not make for constructive politics in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is a reckless thing to do and I do not see how this is in the national interest.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: If the accusers have details and concrete evidence that the Prime Minister has been lying and abusing his power, allowing his wife to influence the appointment of public officials, they should make all of them public by now.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: They should not be waging a continuous media campaign to keep the nation in suspense.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, the Government has also contributed to the squabble.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It does not help that the Prime Minister and some of his Cabinet colleagues have responded in kind on Facebook and even making counter allegations on the motive and character of the other party.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Government should set an example and needs to maintain its dignity in the face of insults to its integrity.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It should not be involved in a Facebook brawl for the whole world to see.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Cabinet members, more than anyone else, should refrain from making insinuations about the character and motivations of the accusers.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Government should not continue with this dispute in the public domain.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Prime Minister is faced with serious allegations from his brother and sister.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: These allegations need to be addressed in a proper manner.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: As the Prime Minister once said himself, "Such matters cannot be just you say, I say.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is the hallmark of the People's Action Party (PAP) Government in the past to get to the bottom of such matters via the Court." I believe that the "you say, I say" exchange will continue in social media if the Prime Minister fails to take action to put a stop to it.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Prime Minister, as he had said earlier in the Ministerial Statement, seems to hope to resolve this issue after this Parliament session.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: But how sure is he that his siblings will not continue to make allegations or adding new allegations against him?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: He is already being accused of trying to cover up and whitewash himself by using Parliament.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Next, it seems to me that the Minister for Law was a close personal friend of Mr Lee Kuan Yew and other members of the Lee family.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: He has now fallen out with some members of the Lee family.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Dr Lee Wei Ling said he was a changed person.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: He was previously involved in giving personal advice relating to Mr Lee Kuan Yew's will.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, he is also now part of the Ministerial Committee which is looking at the issue of the house arising from the will.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, the current Attorney-General (AG), Mr Lucien Wong, was acting as Mr Lee Hsien Loong's personal lawyer in his private dispute against his siblings.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: But now, the same person is in the position to advise the Government and the Cabinet on matters related to the house and Mr Lee Kuan Yew's will.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Was this consideration taken into account when he was appointed the AG?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Can the Prime Minister clarify the role of the Law Minister and the AG in this matter and explain to the House whether there is any conflict of interest?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: If so, how are they going to account to the public for this?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: However, this is not a Korean drama show.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: It is a serious matter because it affects the credibility of our entire country.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The timing of the public blow-up of the private dispute is also unfortunate.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: At this juncture, the country faces serious challenges.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Singapore is facing a tricky and volatile geopolitical situation and the Government has to navigate our small state between a self-centred America and a more assertive China skillfully and carefully.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: We also seem to be vulnerable to the worsening security situation in the war against terrorism in Southeast Asia with troubling cases of self-radicalisation surfacing at home.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: We had only recently embarked on a critical transformation of the Singapore economy and workforce to enable our companies and workers to seize the opportunities of technological disruption to stay competitive.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: We are still fixing persistent problems with our physical and social infrastructure, in particular, the recent continuous major Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) breakdowns.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Although the Prime Minister has said this saga will not affect the work of the Government, I am of the view that it is a serious distraction to the Government in dealing with the serious challenges when the Cabinet members − all of them are not members of the Lee family − but have been unnecessarily drawn into the dispute which, to me, is essentially a family dispute.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Ministers need to focus on rallying Singaporeans to be united in facing the challenges and not be participating in a divisive dispute.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I hope that all necessary steps are taken by the Prime Minister and his Cabinet colleagues to achieve a resolution as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: In this regard, I have a couple of personal suggestions for the Government to consider and hope to end the matter and move on.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Individuals who make less serious allegations that undermine the reputation and authority of the Prime Minister and Cabinet Ministers have been brought to task for libel.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: There is no reason why this time it should be different because it comes from the Lee family.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: In fact, the allegations are much more serious.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Given the past track record, not doing so would risk the Government giving the impression that it is afraid of what the Lee siblings might say or reveal.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: This will taint the trust Singaporeans have placed in the Government and compromise the high standards that the Government prides itself on achieving and aspires to maintain.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Anyway, this Lee family saga playing out on Facebook has become an ugly media circus.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Settling this in Court will enable everyone to put forward their sides of the story with evidence and with dignity.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Government can take the options available under the law by going through the process of assessment to make a decision like any other important heritage sites in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: I believe that, to a large extent, it is the delay in acting which has led to this sorry state of affairs.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: What further deliberations does the Committee intend to make and how much more time does it need to come to a decision?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Some countries which had a high regard for us are laughing at us, and the international media has amplified and maximised the bad publicity on Singapore.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: The Lee family saga has shaken international confidence in Singapore, which is known as a country of political and social stability.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Settle the dispute in the appropriate forum, which is the Court.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Restore the line of distinction between the private and the public.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I suspect that when an individual chooses to look at the world through a distorted lens, there are conspiracies and shadows everywhere.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Much has been said and will be said about this matter, and so, this time, I think I will be terse.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I think it is, therefore, necessary for the Government and Parliament to address these allegations in an open, transparent and fair manner.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As mentioned in the Straits Times, in our tightly knitted Singapore community, when relationships are complex and interwoven, where duties and private relationships intermingle, how do we ensure that there are institutional checks and balances to prevent any abuse?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: This furore has raised many questions in the minds of Singaporeans I have spoken to.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: These are some of the questions that have been directed to the Government as well as to Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Why the rush to prepare and sign the will?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And when Dr Lee Wei Ling claimed that the Prime Minister had, I quote, "angrily threatened to gazette 38 Oxley Road", is there anyone else who can collaborate on this allegation?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: When Dr Lee Wei Ling also alleged that photographers from the Ministry of Communication and Information (MCI) helped Ms Ho Ching photograph and catalogue the late Mr Lee's artefacts, questions arise, like, why documentation must be done when the family is still in a period of grief?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: When Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee alleged, and I quote, "we feel hugely uncomfortable and closely monitored in our country", does Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling have any substantial evidence for these statements?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Did the Government investigate these statements and, if it had, what were the findings?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Were Mr Lee and Dr Lee being interviewed and questioned after they had made these statements?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: When both Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling alleged that the Prime Minister harbours political ambitions for his son Mr Li Hongyi, again, where is the evidence?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What is the Prime Minister's position on this?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Since the Government knew of the dispute within the family, why did the state not let the dispute be settled before considering possible actions for 38 Oxley Road?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What is the reason for the Government's choice for not taking the probate at face value and focus solely on the historic value of the house?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: What is it in this particular case that is beyond the mandate of the Board that they cannot decide or advise and how do we know in future when or whether a Ministerial Committee should be set up to look at preservation of particular sites and monuments?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And in the case of the appointment of Mr Lucien Wong as the AG, was the President formally informed of the current AG's former role as the Prime Minister's personal lawyer?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: If he was informed, then how did the President address this issue of potential conflict of interest?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To me, it means being able to find satisfactory and trustworthy responses to the above questions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It also means all individuals involved should get a fair hearing, their statements carefully studied by an independent panel and these proceedings made fully available to the public as well, precisely because these allegations are serious and that is why we are here today.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Parliament sits here to hear, as we have done, the Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister's elaborate statements and I thank them for it.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But I would state that it now still sounds like a case of "your words against mine and mine against yours".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I believe the public would also want to hear from Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling and all the players involved as well in the same manner as a matter of fairness.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: As such, Parliament might be the right place to air the Government's position but may not be the right place to settle this issue once and for all, as some of the Members have wished for.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, they may have to consider another independent platform that will allow all parties to present their cases.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Some people have spoken of the desire for closure on this issue.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But what kind of closure do we want?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: A good closure is not just about restoring or maintaining faith and confidence in the Government.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is also about the opportunity to scrutinise and interrogate existing systems and structures.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We must ensure this mechanism that we want to hold on to such that it will not be misinterpreted in our efforts in disincubating this issue as a calibrated public relations exercise.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We have to show that the system we have in place are robust, with checks and balances built in to withstand open scrutiny.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: A good closure can only be achieved if our system inspires confidence by being truly transparent and allowing for fair hearing from all sides − Government officials and individual citizens.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is important for Singaporeans to have an unwavering belief in our system of Government.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In a moment of crisis, the resilience of Singapore and our system is at the same time being tested and strengthened.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I have one more point to say and this relates to the emotional aspects of heritage and memory.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We want to remember and preserve things we hold dearly in a specific way.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Some buildings and monuments do not only impact individuals but also the wider community.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Very often, past decisions have been made favouring pragmatism over idealism.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, in this particular case, it is a bit different from the National Library building because the National Library and Bukit Brown Cemetery were public spaces.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But now, we have a private estate where the community believes that it has a lot of historical value.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And how do we then balance the need of the individuals as well as the state?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Will the closure we all seek ever be fully realised?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Many elderly people I meet through the course of my work on end-of-life issues share with me stories about their wills.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Although they know what they want, they are very apprehensive and worry about how other family members would think.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: When I asked them if they have discussed the matter with their family members, they said it is difficult to talk about such things.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Family does not always have a beautiful utopian image that we like to conjure.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Where there are disputes, how do we repair a broken relationship?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Honestly, I do not know if it is ever possible, because in our Chinese saying, we have said this, "破 镜 难 圆 ", that is, "a broken mirror can never come together".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The last words of the play ring very loudly, "The weight of this sad time we must obey.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Speak what we feel, not what we ought to say.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We that are young shall never see so much, nor live so long." I hope this incident, whatever its final decision, will only strengthen our resolve to make Singapore exist and its system even more robust, open and transparent.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Before I proceed to call the next Member, let me just remind Members that the debate is on (a) Alleged Abuse of Power on 38 Oxley Road; and (b) the Ministerial Committee on 38 Oxley Road.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, let us confine the debate to the integrity of the Government, its processes, institutions and leadership and not talk about the merits of the family dispute.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   Firstly, please allow me to wish you Selamat Hari Raya, Mdm Speaker, and I also seek your forgiveness, and to all Members in this House and Muslim Singaporeans, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Over the past few weeks, an unexpected development caught many Singaporeans by surprise.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The quarrel between siblings from the family of Singapore's founder, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, was made public and affected all of us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is especially since the allegations were mainly aimed towards the eldest son of Mr Lee, who is also the Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is more serious are the allegations levelled by his own siblings that are certainly hard to ignore and instead should be addressed properly without making matters worse.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Within the Malay community, based on my own observations and conversations, many have expressed concern and are quite uncomfortable with matters like having a family quarrel so openly.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some felt that it is a private matter and should be resolved within the family itself, based on some of the issues that were raised.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some are confused, some have raised questions, and some have queried how such a quarrel could happen.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To them, in line with our cultural values, it is not good to talk about such matters.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What more when it involves the family of a leader who is renowned and beyond compare?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As children, it is our responsibility to protect our family's good name, regardless of their position.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, we should understand that this is not a trivial dispute, because it involves issues of national interest and also involves our Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Most importantly, Singaporeans should know the true facts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With that, they can decide for themselves why this dispute is brought to the open now because all it does is confuse matters further to the point that it affects the reputation of the Government and Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our limited resources should not be spent on addressing issues that essentially should not have been raised until it becomes the focus of the Government, especially since we are facing many national challenges.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am moved by the Prime Minister's apology, as well as his explanations and clarifications about the actual situation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is clearly difficult for the Prime Minister, seeing that he is the Prime Minister and also the eldest son of Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Others who are involved in this issue are also prominent people and have served in various capacities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: That is why today's session is very important.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is important for us to address four main issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, should the Government involve itself with the issue of who prepared the last will?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Thirdly, whether there was any conflict of interest in the issue of the Deed of Gift.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, is the 38 Oxley Road issue such an important matter that it requires a Ministerial-level committee?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In the Prime Minister's speech just now, he has convinced the people that the Government acted independently of the Prime Minister, especially since it has to make a decision in which the Prime Minister himself has a personal stake.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singaporeans' views about the residence at 38 Oxley Road have been mixed.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Tradition teaches us to respect the wishes of the late Mr Lee and the wishes of the family.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: However, the house is not any house, and its historical significance has evoked an emotional response from many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many have also voiced out and wrote in for the house to be preserved.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, we can understand why the Government took into account and considered the historical significance of the house and explore options for the house.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister, who also chairs the Ministerial Committee, have explained further about the role of this committee and why it was studying family matters, even though the late Mr Lee had several times stated his desire for the house to be demolished.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If the Government's position is that no decision needs to be made as long as Dr Lee Wei Ling still resides there, why was there a hurry to form this committee?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are other matters regarding the potential value of the site of the house and the Government's jurisdiction about preserving the house as a heritage.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Otherwise, incorrect facts and allegations can confuse many people.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As long as no final decision needs to be made until it is time to do so, what is the actual intention of making this dispute public?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What is the real motivation behind this unhappiness?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This can confuse the people and should be resolved honestly before it becomes prolonged.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The house, the family involved, and even the institutions and laws created regarding matters like land acquisition and heritage protection, are all the legacy of the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, I reckon that Singaporeans do not wish to see these institutions and legacy become tainted by this dispute.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): Mdm Speaker, the last couple of weeks have been a difficult one for many Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As we deal with the information being shared by both parties on social media, we also had to contend with the country's history, systems and reputation being questioned in the international media − a source of concern and, sometimes, embarrassment to many Singaporeans I spoke to.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, why is this matter being debated now?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And we are left puzzled as to what is the underlying motivation behind this dispute.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If the Government has committed not to make a decision at this point in time and not on behalf of the government of the future, then what are this dispute and the public allegations all about?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Is it just about the house or is there more to this?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The other concern is a question of principle.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For decades, many regular Singaporeans have had their homes and land acquired for the greater national good.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some for development of Housing and Development Board flats or MRT lines, while others for heritage and preservation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So many others have sacrificed − not everyone willingly − for the greater good and national interest.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Based on the Prime Minister's Statement earlier, I can only guess that the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew recognised and respected this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Otherwise, he could have left out the second part of paragraph 7 of his will or deliberated the demolishment of the home while he was still alive.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Regardless of the motivations and timing, this issue has raised many questions, particularly certain allegations against the Prime Minister and the Government of abuse of power.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I would like to know if these allegations had an ounce of truth and I trust that this Parliamentary session must shed light because Singaporeans want to know the truth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand that Ministerial Committees are common and the Cabinet has assembled them on many strategic matters.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But was the case of 38 Oxley Road such an important issue that it required assembling a Ministerial Committee?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would it not have sufficed to have URA, NHB or any other relevant Government agency assess the matter and give its recommendations to the Cabinet instead?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And if, indeed, it was necessary, then Singaporeans deserve to know if the Committee was indeed independent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because the fact that you have to make a decision on the matter where their boss has personal interest does raise questions, but I think the Prime Minister has already also spoken that you have to trust the Cabinet and the Government to remain independent.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister, too, has also shared in his Ministerial Statement of the roles and functions of the Ministerial Committee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But the question I have would be that the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew had mentioned on many occasions that he wanted the house demolished.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What else transpired when he met the Cabinet on 21 July 2011?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Government has said that it did not need to make a decision now as Dr Lee Wei Ling is still staying there.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If so, was there a reason to set up the Ministerial Committee now?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And how has the Committee interpreted paragraph 7 of the will thus far?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under what circumstances or criteria can the Government declare a house a national monument for preservation to prevent any demolition or redevelopment while the family chooses to live onsite?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In its study, what does the Committee estimate to be the potential value of the site, if sold, given the current zoning of the area?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second area, Madam, that requires clarification is the Deed of Gift.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Due to the allegations that have been made, many Singaporeans deserve to know when the Prime Minister came to know of the Deed and if there was any leak outside of the purview.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And I think the Minister has addressed that earlier.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here, the role of NHB comes into question.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Why did NHB sign on to take over the items, despite the onerous contractual obligations and knowing that there could be potentially a family dispute?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Since there was potentially a conflict of interest in the matter of Ms Lee Suet Fern, who served on the NHB board and whose firm had prepared the contract on behalf of the family, then why did NHB go ahead and sign it?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Was it under any pressure to do so, as you have a Board of Directors working the agreement?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given that many of our top talent in Singapore wear multiple hats, how can we enhance the governance of our Government agencies to avoid potential conflict of interest in future?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many Singaporeans wonder why it is necessary for the Government to be involved in ascertaining the accuracy of the will, if at all.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Should it not be a private matter, to be challenged in Court, they ask?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are also some quarters who see the Government taking a role in this because the Prime Minister came out to say that he has "grave concerns" on the preparation of the last will.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, on the platform that has been chosen for this matter, as mentioned by Members, some Singaporeans have asked if a Ministerial Statement in Parliament was the right platform to address this issue.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While I agree that the integrity of the Government should be defended, I hope that we all also realise that this may not stop further allegations from being hurled at the Government.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have already seen, just in the past few days alone, how new actors have been brought into the fray − both Ministers and public servants − as the allegations grew.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I urge all members of the family to take a more private course from here on to address this dispute.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Opening it up into the public domain does not serve Singapore's interest at all, as it only tarnishes the country's reputation, something that no Singaporean would want and, not least, the late Mr Lee himself.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If the family wishes to honour his wishes and legacy, then this would be a good base to start from.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But to be fair to the Prime Minister, are the allegations outrageous?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Are they merely a figment of the Lee siblings' overactive imagination?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We in this House will not be able to get down to the bottom of these questions during this debate for one simple reason − there is no natural justice in the procedure adopted.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: With due respect to the Prime Minister, we are only hearing the Prime Minister's version, the Government's version, today.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What else there is, we do not know.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, allegations have been made today that the Lee siblings have been selective in their documentation and may not have been truthful.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am not accusing the Prime Minister of lying.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I am simply stating what we all know − that we simply do not have full information to confidently decide on who and what to believe.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Notwithstanding the limited value of this session, I wish to raise one matter that should be of concern to every Singaporean who wishes to see Singapore as a bastion that upholds the rule of law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And, that is, how fundamentally precious it is that we defend with all our hearts and minds the independence of our Organs of State?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We must protect the Organs of State as professional bodies with a national mission.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Government should never seek to interfere with or to influence those Organs of State set up to ensure good governance.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: AGO prides itself in its Core Values of Independence and Integrity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In elaborating on its independence, the AGO states that it carries out its audits without fear or favour.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In explaining its Integrity, the AGO pledges to strive to uphold the public trust in its work.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Such a lofty mission is fleshed out in the AGO's annual reports, which document publicly the financial management shortcomings of Ministries and PMO.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The significant contribution of AGO towards good governance and public accountability is clear to all of us.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I now turn to another Organ of State, the AG's Chambers (AGC).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: According to the AGC website, the AGC recognises that "As principal legal adviser to the Government, the AG plays an important role in upholding the rule of law in Singapore, and thus contributes to one of the key aspirations of her people: to build a democratic society based on the fundamental ideals of justice and equality".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: When Judges decide cases, they are constrained by the laws passed by Parliament, and their decisions are public and appealable.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: He can decide not to charge a person who has committed an offence, to let an offender off with a warning, to reduce charges and so on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These decisions are most weighty, yet they are not public and not appealable.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is not an exaggeration to say that all of us are at the mercy of the AG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But each of us should be fairly treated by him since, under the Constitution, all of us are equal before the law and entitled to the equal protection of the law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Even though the AG is constitutionally a member of the Executive, he is expected to work independently.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is stated on the AGC website that the AG, in his role as public prosecutor, "is vested with the power to institute, conduct or discontinue proceedings for any offence.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The AG is independent in this role, and not subject to the control of the Government".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, past Law Ministers had expressly endorsed the need for there to be distance between the Government and AGC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For instance, Prof S Jayakumar recently gave an interview for a book marking AGC's 150th Anniversary.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There, he recalled how when he was appointed Minister of State for Law in 1981, he was given an office located at AGC, then in High Street.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Prof Jayakumar then recounted as follows: "I told the then AG Tan Boon Teik that it was not proper for a Minister of State for Law to be housed in AGC because it would raise all sorts of questions about the AGC's autonomy." Fast forward to today.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In prior debates this year, I had raised questions about the appointment of the current AG and his newest Deputy AG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The role of the newest Deputy AG as an immediate past MP is well-known.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Now, there is no legal prohibition on appointing the Government's close friends and former party comrades as the AG or Deputy AG.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But, from a system point of view, do these appointments instill public confidence that the AGC will act independently in matters where the Government, or worse, the Prime Minister, has an interest in the outcomes?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the time when the appointments were being considered, were there no other qualified persons to take up those posts?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What about the many career Legal Service officers who had dedicated their lives to public service?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Coming back to facts at hand, I am concerned about the conflicts of interest.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: How will the AGC act in advising the Government on any decisions it wishes to take on 38 Oxley Road?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Has the AGC already been giving advice to the Committee, and who within the AGC is giving the advice?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I understand that he only recently resigned as a cadre member of the PAP.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Will he recuse himself from the matter, too, since his former party leader, the Secretary-General, is personally involved?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: One consistent theme is embarrassment at the public airing of family disputes and that family matters should be settled privately.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: When allegations are made against Organs of State, that they cower to personalities, that they are subservient to personalities, then I begin to take those allegations very seriously.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have spent my adult life in Organs of State.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I happened to have served in four − a judicial officer in the Supreme Court, then posted to the AGC and, thereafter, appointments in the State Courts and the Supreme Court, and now, Parliament.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In each office, I have never made the mission of the Organ of State subservient to any personality − never.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In every Organ of State I have worked in, we worked toward a higher mission − the good of a working, functional Singapore − for generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, for me, it is the allegations against the Organs of State that have migrated this family issue from the private domain into the sphere of public debate.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And so, we are here today, in Parliament, to get to the bottom of these allegations, extract answers and determine their veracity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Not a pleasant exercise, but one that is required.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I will focus on the allegations first, and then, will pose a series of questions arising from the allegations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I will focus on the allegations surrounding the misuse of Organs of State and abuse of power.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I think it is better that I do not weigh in on the aspects of the will because I am a partner at Lee & Lee.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am a lawyer at Lee & Lee and declare that for the Hansard record.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, let us get on with the allegations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: On 29 June 2017 at 5.25 pm, Mr Lee Hsien Yang said this on Facebook: "We have serious concerns with Lee Hsien Loong's attempt to cover up and whitewash himself in Parliament on 3 July.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We have begun to show evidence of his misuse of his position and influence to drive his personal agenda.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This Parliamentary session is a forum that again places Hsien Loong before his subordinates.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They lack both sufficient background and evidence of the numerous instances of abuse and conflicts of interest, many yet to be raised.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Historically, few PAP MPs have dared to dissent even when the Party Whip was lifted.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There will be no opportunity or adequate time for evidence to be properly drawn together, placed before Parliament, and considered.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Indeed, it could also be an opportunity to continue to mislead or insinuate under this privilege." The allegation infers that there are issues that need to be addressed that may not have, as of yet, surfaced.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do not want to prejudge the situation.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is my hope that whatever can be addressed at this session be addressed, that is, all that have been brought up since 14 June and whatever else Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling could launch.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Deal with the whole lot now, instead of having to reconvene if future and different allegations are made.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With that, I would like to ask some questions pertaining to the crux of the allegations.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The first set of questions is relating to the Government as a whole.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Fourth, they continued to say, "They see many upright leaders of quality and integrity throughout the Public Service who are constrained by Hsien Loong's misuse of power at the very top." Is it true that the Public Service is constrained by the Prime Minister's misuse of power at the top?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Fifth, is it true or false that the leadership and direction of the Government is directed for personal purposes or any other improper purpose?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Sixth, is it true or false that Organs of State may be used for personal agendas?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The seventh set of questions is about the Cabinet and the Ministerial Committee.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Is it true or false that the Ministerial Committee is merely a facade and that the Prime Minister is able to influence it one way or the other?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Eighth, is it true or false that the Ministerial Committee never told Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling about options they were exploring?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Tenth, on 14 June 2017, Mr Lee Hsien Yang said, "Hsien Loong has asserted to the Committee that Lee Kuan Yew would 'accept any decision by the Government to preserve 38 Oxley Road.'… In doing this, Hsien Loong has deliberately misrepresented Lee Kuan Yew's clear intentions for his own political benefit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: He has also gone back on his own declarations that he would recuse himself from all Government decisions involving 38 Oxley." Is it true or false that the Prime Minister has misguided a Ministerial Committee to fulfil his own personal purposes?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These series of questions are questions that are drawn from the multiple allegations thrown at the Organs of State, the Prime Minister and his office.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is my view that no mission of an Organ of State in Singapore should lay subservient to a personality.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Its mission to serve the electorate must never be compromised or seen to be compromised.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such rigour brings accountability, such accountability brings trust, such trust ensures productive leadership, and such productive leadership brings about a working, functional Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Today is an example of the rubric for accountability.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Before I close, I want to say this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have worked with the Prime Minister for a number of years now, and I have never had cause to doubt his integrity and loyalty to the country.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It has been, and I trust, will always be, Singapore first, for him.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But the debate's robustness is not only to advantage all Singaporeans to get to the bottom of the facts but it is also to show jurisdictions and the press worldwide that we allow facts to speak for themselves in this House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Much has been said by the foreign press about this kerfuffle.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The New York Times, SCMP, Cable News Network (CNN) have gleefully covered this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is my hope that the responses will put an end to the doubts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Then, we can steer Singapore back to important affairs of the state.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I note that the dispute has been covered in the international press, including the unproven allegations about the Prime Minister and our system.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The whole affair has tarnished the reputation of our Government as clean and altruistic.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is precisely the reputation that the late Minister Mentor Lee spent his whole life building.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If he were alive, he would be deeply hurt by the quarrelling of his children in public.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many of my residents have been discussing this issue.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many wonder why the siblings took such private issues to the public.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Today, on behalf of my residents, I would like to raise three issues.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Ms Lim Suet Fern was asking NHB to accept the terms which are bad for NHB and misleading the public.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is this acceptable conduct for Morgan Lewis, Suet Fern as lawyer and NHB Board Member?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many asked, "What is the quarrel all about?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Who drafted the will?" Mr Lee Hsien Yang said it was drafted by Ms Kwa Kim Li.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We do not even know who drafted the will.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If so, why not just come out and admit it?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Why does he try and deny that his wife drafted it when emails seem clear?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What has the Committee done that Mr Lee Hsien Yang claimed that he was "pushed into a corner"?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In yesterday's Straits Times, Hsien Yang said that he would not want to preserve the house nor would he want to build a condominium because it would not be in accordance with Minister Mentor Lee's values.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Does that not sound a lot like what Deputy Prime Minister Teo said − that he would not support the two extremes of total preservation and letting the public in, and building private residences on the other hand?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   Many residents told me that this dispute was bad for both Singapore and Mr Lee Kuan Yew's reputation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They asked me what this whole thing was about.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They specifically wanted to ask why some basic facts cannot be shared with Singaporeans in full and truthfully.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: For example, with regard to Mr Lee Kuan Yew's Memorial Exhibition, Mr Lee Hsien Yang and Dr Lee Wei Ling set conditions that only the first half of the demolition clause of the will can be displayed and, the second half, which considered the possibility of preserving the house, cannot be displayed.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another example is relating to who drafted the last will.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Lee Hsien Yang said it was drafted by Kwa Kim Lee but she denied it.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, their email shows that Mr Lee Hsien Yang's wife, Ms Lim Suet Fern, was involved in the drafting.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Why would Mr Lee Hsien Yang deny it?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think if Mr Lee Kuan Yew were alive, he would definitely not want him to confuse the facts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Another question − Mr Lee Hsien Yang said he did not want to preserve the house nor have it redeveloped into a condominium.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo also said that he personally did not support the two extreme options, that is, to preserve the house and open to the public on one end, or to redevelop it into a private building on the other.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It seemed that they shared the same view.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Then why would Mr Lee Hsien Yang make it into the gossip of the town?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: He should have done what the Prime Minister did – give statutory statement to the Ministerial Committee and then let the Committee decide.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Why would he rather damage the reputation of his family and his country than doing so?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
